# Field Kettle, 1.2 litre

This is a kettle for the stove you carry. It holds 1.2 litres, enough for two mugs of tea and a pot of porridge, and weighs 310 grams empty. The body is hard-anodised aluminium, 0.8 mm thick, finished with a rolled lip so it pours cleanly instead of dribbling down the side. The lid sits in a groove and stays put when you tip the kettle to pour.

The handle folds flat against the body and locks open with a steel pin. Silicone wraps it to the knuckle, so you can lift the kettle off a gas burner without a glove. The spout has a hinged cap that whistles at a rolling boil. Take the cap off and it pours faster, which helps when filling a bottle.

On a 2,000-watt canister stove, 1 litre of water at 15 degrees boils in four minutes and ten seconds at sea level. At 3,000 metres it took us five and a half minutes. The ribbed base spreads the heat and keeps the kettle from rocking on a small burner head. It will not work on an induction hob.

The kettle nests inside the 1.8 litre pot from the same range, and a 230 gram gas canister fits inside the kettle with the lid on. A mesh bag is included, but it is not a dry bag and will not keep soot off your sleeping bag. Pack the kettle in the bag and the bag in an outside pocket.

Wash it by hand. A steel scourer will scratch the anodised finish, and a dishwasher will dull it. Never boil the kettle dry: the handle wrap is rated to 230 degrees, and the aluminium will warp above that.

The kettle is guaranteed for two years against faults in materials and manufacture. Dents from drops and rocks are not faults. If you lose the lid or the handle pin, each is sold separately for two pounds, post paid.

Sizes: 1.2 litre (this page), 1.8 litre and 2.5 litre. Colours: grey and green. Made in Portugal.
